channel.title: Stanford HAI News
channel.description: AI research, policy, and societal impact news from Stanford HAI

item.title: Want Employees to Embrace AI? Stop Selling It as a Productivity Tool
item.description: How managers introduce and support AI determines whether workers engage with or resist the technology.

item.title: Stanford HAI Welcomes 15 New HAI Data Science Scholars
item.description: The two-year fellowship supports PhD researchers across law, medicine, physics, statistics, education, and engineering.

item.title: The Tests That Grade AI May Be Getting It Wrong
item.description: Benchmarks — the standardized tests that rank AI models on safety, bias, and reasoning — drive markets and shape regulation. New Stanford research finds they often don't measure what they claim to.

item.title: Can AI Be Slowed Down? Stanford HAI Experts Weigh the Risks, Rules and Race Ahead
item.description: In a new series called Prompt Response, Stanford’s Surya Ganguli, Diyi Yang and Rob Reich examined emergent agent behavior, recursive self-improvement, independent evaluation and whether a kill switch can make advanced AI safer.

item.title: AI Legal Review Says Millions Live Under Discriminatory Local Laws
item.description: Building an AI pipeline to comb through millions of local statutes, researchers at Stanford Law School turn a spotlight on unsavory laws still on the books in communities across the country.

item.title: Your ‘For You’ Algorithm Disagrees With You
item.description: A new Stanford-led study finds that X’s “For You” algorithm mistakes outrage for interest – and fills your feed accordingly.

item.title: Companies That Buy and Sell Your Data Are Not Following California’s Strict Privacy Laws
item.description: A new Stanford study shows data brokers are making it difficult for consumers to submit privacy requests and failing to report how many privacy requests they receive.

item.title: New Stanford Grants Tackle AI's Impact on Global Security and Geopolitics
item.description: Stanford HAI and the Hoover Institution’s Technology Policy Accelerator back projects examining AI's role in detecting nuclear proliferation, U.S.-China competition, and political influence.

item.title: AI Companions May Worsen Loneliness for Vulnerable Users, Stanford Study Finds
item.description: Stanford research finds that users with limited social networks who seek emotional support from AI companions experience lower well-being.

item.title: Open-Weight Models Aren’t Enough. We Need Truly Open Source AI Models for Science and Society.
item.description: As Chinese AI closes the capability gap, Washington and Silicon Valley debate open-weight models. Stanford HAI's James Landay says it's the right conversation framed the wrong way.

item.title: Why Governing World Models Is AI's Next Big Policy Challenge
item.description: As artificial intelligence moves beyond language into the physical world through "world models," Stanford researchers warn that policymakers face an even steeper governance challenge than with large language models—and the window to get ahead of the technology is closing fast.

item.title: The Complexities of Governing Mental Health AI
item.description: Policymakers, academics, healthcare providers, AI developers, and patient advocates convened by Stanford HAI identify critical gaps in how we regulate AI tools used for therapy and emotional support.

item.title: How AI Is Helping States Cut Through Decades of Red Tape
item.description: Stanford researchers scanned 500 million words of state law to reveal the stunning growth of reporting requirements, and are now giving governments a tool to clean them up.

item.title: Legal AI’s Legibility Problem
item.description: Increasing reliance on language models for legal tasks have led to calls for more information about the likelihood and severity of potential errors. Realizing useful and robust transparency requires an institutional perspective, say the editors of a new special section in PNAS.

item.title: The AI Sovereignty Paradox: Should Countries Buy, Build, or Lease to Maintain Strategic Control of Their AI?
item.description: As nations invest billions to reduce reliance on foreign AI providers, a new Stanford HAI report surveys commercial sovereignty solutions and assesses the extent to which they meaningfully reduce dependencies on U.S. tech giants.

item.title: Stanford Study Exposes Major Flaw in AI Mental Health Safety Testing
item.description: With increased use of chatbots in mental health contexts, AI developers now rely on human experts to evaluate AI’s responses for “safety” – but experts rarely agree on what’s safe.

item.title: Stanford Scientists Build an AI Lab Partner
item.description: Biomni can analyze mountains of medical data, spot patterns humans might miss, and even design experiments—helping researchers make discoveries faster in the race to cure disease.

item.title: Advancing Sustainability Through Data Science: Conference Highlights
item.description: Advancing Sustainability Through Data Science: Conference Highlights
